m1.note: Raises bus factor and scope-vs-capacity concerns and speculates some surfaces are thinner than advertised, but makes no claim that code is unreviewed, unaudited, or shipped too fast for scrutiny — it actually praises the CI/security tooling.

m2.quote: Writing your own authorization server is a decision most teams should be talked out of.
m2.note: Explicitly frames the built-in OAuth 2.1 server as home-grown auth that should be delegated, and asks whether an existing IdP can be used instead.

m3.note: Engages directly with the published benchmark and DOIs, criticizing them as circular, ceiling-effect, small-n and vendor-self-published rather than claiming evidence is absent.

m4.note: Correctly credits the PostgreSQL-only deployment shape and scopes DataHub/Trino to the 'full experience' rather than treating it as a hard requirement or lock-in.
